# Balcony Tomatoes

## Setup

The south-facing balcony gets sun from about nine in the morning until five in the afternoon, which is the whole reason this works. I set out five 30 L grow bags along the railing, each filled with a peat-free compost mix and a handful of slow release feed. I picked a compact cordon variety bred for containers, plus a bush type, so the cropping is not all at once. A cane tripod in every bag keeps the stems upright once fruit sets, and I tie them in with soft twine so nothing cuts the skin. Drainage holes at the base sit clear of the tray so roots never stand in water.

## Watering

In July each plant drinks 5 L daily, poured slowly at the base in the morning so the leaves stay dry overnight. I check the top two centimetres of compost with a finger before I water; if it is already damp I skip a day. A high-potassium feed goes in weekly once the first truss sets, diluted to half strength, and I stop feeding when the evening temperatures drop. Drip trays catch the runoff and I empty them so nothing stagnates. On windy days I water twice, since the bags dry out fast up there.

## Harvest

Picking starts in late July with the first ripe tomatoes, and after that I go round every second morning with a bowl. I watch for blight from August, when humid nights and warm days make it inevitable on an exposed balcony; any brown patch on a stem means cutting the plant back hard. Green fruit at the end of the season ripens on a windowsill indoors. The plants get pulled and the compost goes on the flower border once the last pod is picked.
